name: Malabar Parotta
steps: Mix flour, sugar and salt. Add water and 15 ml oil; knead vigorously for 10–12 minutes until very smooth and stretchy rather than sticky.
Coat dough with 5 ml oil and rest covered for 1 hour. Divide into eight balls, lightly oil and rest another 20 minutes.
Oil the worktop lightly. Stretch each ball into a very thin sheet using oiled hands; small tears are acceptable. Spread a little measured oil over it.
Pleat the sheet into a long ribbon, coil loosely and tuck the end underneath. Rest the coils covered for 15 minutes before gently flattening to 15 cm.
Cook on a medium-hot heavy tawa for about 2 minutes per side, using remaining oil sparingly. Flip repeatedly until layered edges are cooked and golden spots form.
Stack two or three hot parottas and press their edges inward with clean cloth-covered hands to separate the layers. Serve immediately while tender inside.
tips: Keep unused dough covered so the surface does not dry out.
notes: Makes eight layered parottas. This traditional-style version uses flour, water and oil without added dairy.
